Detector.Details: Finds methods that read caloric properties of a phase or fluid without first initialising it.

BugPattern.ShortDescription: Caloric property read without init(2) or higher in the same method
BugPattern.LongDescription: {1} reads a caloric property ({2}) of a phase or fluid without first calling init(2) or higher, initProperties(), initThermoProperties(), initPhysicalProperties(), a ThermodynamicOperations flash or run() earlier in the method
BugPattern.Details:
A TP flash leaves the phases at init level 1, where only fugacities are valid. Enthalpy, entropy, Cp, Cv and the other caloric properties are built from temperature and pressure derivatives that belong to the last init(2) or init(3) call, so reading them after a TP flash can silently return values for an older state.

Call init(2) (or higher), initProperties(), initThermoProperties() or initPhysicalProperties() on the fluid before reading the property, or run the owning unit first. If the fluid is guaranteed to be initialised by the caller, record the finding in the reviewed rules baseline instead of suppressing it.

BugPattern.ShortDescription: Repeated init call on the same fluid with nothing changed in between
BugPattern.LongDescription: {1} calls {2} on a fluid that was already initialised by an identical call earlier in the method, with no call, store or branch in between that could have changed it
BugPattern.Details:
Initialisation calls such as init(3), initProperties() and initPhysicalProperties() recalculate all phases and are among the most expensive calls in a process model. Repeating an identical call on the same fluid, with no change to temperature, pressure, composition or a flash in between, only costs computation time.

Remove the second call. If only one property is needed, initialise just that property, for example initPhysicalProperties("density"), which is faster than a full initialisation.

BugPattern.ShortDescription: Physical property read without initialising it in the same method
BugPattern.LongDescription: {1} reads a physical property ({2}) of a phase or fluid without first initialising it with initPhysicalProperties(), a targeted initPhysicalProperties(name), initProperties() or run() earlier in the method
BugPattern.Details:
Density, viscosity, thermal conductivity, diffusion coefficients and interfacial tension are calculated by the physical property models, not by the equation of state. They are only valid after the physical properties have been initialised for the current temperature, pressure and composition, and an earlier flash does not update them.

When only one of density, viscosity or thermal conductivity is needed, initialise just that property, which is the fastest option: initPhysicalProperties("viscosity") or the PhysicalPropertyType overload. The check accepts a targeted call only for the property it names. Diffusion coefficients and interfacial tension have no targeted initialisation and need initPhysicalProperties(), initProperties() or calcInterfaceProperties(). Running the owning unit first also initialises them. If the fluid is guaranteed to be initialised by the caller, record the finding in the reviewed rules baseline instead of suppressing it.
